A vertex is called a cut vertex (or articulation point) if its removal from the graph, along with its incident edges, increases the number of connected components.

Content:

A vertex [MATH: v] is called a cut vertex (or an articulation point) of a graph [MATH: G] if removing this vertex, along with its incident edges, increases the number of connected components. The graph with vertex [MATH: v] removed is denoted by [MATH: G-v.]

First, notice that our graph has two connected components.

Next, we examine the vertices of the graph one by one.

  • Vertex [MATH: v_3] is not a cut vertex since [MATH: G - v_3] has the same number of connected components as the initial graph.

  • Vertex [MATH: v_5] is a cut vertex. Removing this vertex from the graph, along with its incident edges, increases the number of connected components. The graph [MATH: G - v_5] has three connected components.

  • Vertex [MATH: v_8] is not a cut vertex since [MATH: G - v_8] has the same number of connected components as the initial graph.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
